anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three Ethernet status LEDs D20 (yellow), D25 (green) and D41 (green) sit only on net /NET0098. That net has no other connection, so it is not tied to +3V3, GND or any driven signal. Their cathodes go through R72, R24 and R26 to the Module2 nLED outputs.
anomalies.expected: Every other indicator LED in this netlist has its anode on a supply (for example D36 and D47 on +3V3, D22 on a logic output). The common anode of these three LEDs should be tied to +3V3 so that the active-low nLED outputs can drive them. As built, the LEDs have no supply and cannot light.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity indicator LEDs never illuminate, so the status indication for the CM4 network port is lost. The rest of the board is unaffected.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers (U3 and U50, CA-IS3050G / ISO1050 pinout) have GND2 (pin 5) on the main GND net. GND1 (pin 4) is also on GND. The secondary (bus-side) ground therefore has no separate isolated return, and the isolation barrier is bypassed.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses. Isolation requires the bus-side transceiver ground (GND2, pin 5) and the bus-side supply (VCC2) to be referenced to an isolated ground, separate from the logic GND.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller

anomalies.impact: The CAN bus is not galvanically isolated from the logic and power ground, so ground loops or faults on the bus can reach the CM4 side.

parsed.summary: The most likely defect is that the common anode net /NET0098 of three Ethernet status LEDs is connected to nothing, so those LEDs cannot be powered. A lower-confidence concern is that both CAN isolator GND2 pins are tied to the main GND, which defeats the isolation the spec describes.
